_comment: ei-json baseline digest for the axibridge byte-identity guard (M17 Task 2). See ei-byte-identity.test.mjs for the regeneration procedure. Regenerated 2026-08-27. The baseline had gone STALE for the SECOND time -- it was last captured during MPVE, which landed in v1.5.0, and six releases (v1.5.0 -> v1.7.1) moved the document without anyone recapturing it. It stayed hidden because main's Linux job dies earlier, at the version-sync gate, and never reaches the Node SDK tests at all. Anchor verified rather than assumed: a v1.5.0 (7a4e8fa) build reproduces the OLD recorded digest exactly (3658140 / 4c53bf51...), which is what pins the drift window. The drift is +9,350 chars, attributed by top-level key: players +7,940, buffMap +808, personalDamageMods +369 (new in v1.7.1) and skillMap +211. The players growth is entirely inside `support` and adds NO new player-level keys -- it is the v1.6.x arcdps-parity cleanse buckets (condiCleanseArcdps, boonStripsArcdps*, condiCleanseMinions, ...). Crucially for axibridge, nothing it already consumes changed: every leaf value of the old document was compared against the new one -- 373,534 values, of which 52 moved, and all 52 are skillMap.sNNN.name going "Skill NNN" -> a real name (s1066 -> Resurrect, s30498 -> Resolve, s12854 -> Ice Whirl Combo, ...), which is the v1.6.2 SkillIDs.cs symbol rung. Zero values regressed and zero keys went missing. Determinism was confirmed per this test's own mandate: two consecutive captures at the recorded sourceCommit agree on both length and sha256. sourceCommit is now a full sha, not a branch name -- the previous entry ("mpve-pve-encounter-identification") was a branch that had been deleted after merge, so the anchor it named was unresolvable when this drift was finally investigated.
